blogs.title: Mixed Motives and the 'Central Reason' Standard: Jimenez v. Bondi and the Nexus Requirement
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Tenth Circuit's application of the 'at least one central reason' nexus test in a mixed-motive asylum claim. It examines how the court distinguished between threats arising from the Petitioners' political campaigning and the escalated violence stemming from a property dispute with a narco-trafficker, ultimately finding the political opinion was tangential to the primary motive for harm.

blogs.title: Beyond Threats: The 10th Circuit's Rigid Definition of Persecution in Jimenez
blogs.description: Focusing on the 'past persecution' element, this commentary explores the court's refusal to categorize threats and psychological distress as sufficient persecution without physical harm. It discusses the cumulative effects doctrine and how recent Tenth Circuit precedents like Karki and Chhetri continue to set a high bar for what constitutes 'suffering or harm' under the INA.

blogs.title: The Duty to Report and Internal Relocation: High Hurdles for Asylum Seekers in Jimenez
blogs.description: This post covers the court's rejection of the 'unable or unwilling' government protection argument and the internal relocation analysis. It highlights the evidentiary burden on petitioners to report crimes to local authorities to prove state complicity and discusses the factors the court considered in deeming relocation within Colombia reasonable despite alleged ties between persecutors and the government.
